clue.text: Destructive insect from place close to croft

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: locus is Latin for place, used in English for a site or position
the last letter of croft

explanation.surface: A crop-eating pest has come from somewhere near a small Scottish farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are grasshoppers that swarm and strip crops bare, the classic ruinous pest.

clue.text: Slowly describing a skillion

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so one word encircles the other

blocks.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is gradually explaining what a skillion is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometry sense of drawing a line round something. Skillion is an Australian word for a lean-to roof or shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillion is a single-sloped roof or outbuilding propped against a wall, which is a lean-to.

clue.text: Chapter on Italian region and English county

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another is placed above it

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A book chapter about an Italian region and an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county in the north-west of England, home of the Lake District.

clue.text: Salvation Army girl in steam bath

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army girl relaxing in a steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a Finnish-style hot room where people sit to sweat, a steam bath.

clue.text: Don't agree with article

blocks.note: first meaning: the verb, to protest or disagree
second meaning: the noun, a thing or item

explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests grammar or a newspaper piece, but here it just means an item.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to raise a protest; as a noun it means a physical thing or item.

clue.text: Party head quick to embrace English

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one word wraps round another

blocks.note: bean is slang for the head
fast means quick
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A party leader rushes to hug an English person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party head' looks like a leader, but party is the definition. A beanfeast is British slang for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast, or beano, is a British word for a festive party or celebration meal.

clue.text: European queen, clever, calm and even-tempered

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
QU is an abbreviation for queen
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A European monarch who is bright, serene and good-natured.
explanation.definitionFit: An equable person is placid and not easily upset, so of steady temper.

clue.text: It is twice raised by an Italian artist

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word means writing it bottom to top

blocks.note: the word it, used twice over
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is lifted up twice by a painter from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian painter of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Troops surrounding our arsenal

indicators.note: surrounding means one word goes round another, which sits inside it

blocks.note: an army is a body of troops
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand guard around the weapons store that belongs to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a place where weapons and ammunition are stored.

clue.text: Red-tops in cowardly campaign

blocks.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
to press for something is to campaign for it

explanation.surface: Tabloid newspapers running a gutless crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-tops is British slang for tabloid papers, from their red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow press is sensationalist journalism, the same thing as Britain's tabloid red-tops.

clue.text: A channel, after six, showing a type of bridge

indicators.note: after tells us which piece is written second, following the other

blocks.note: six in Roman numerals
taken as written
a duct is a tube or channel for fluid or air

explanation.surface: A TV channel airing something after six o'clock features a kind of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' and 'six' suggest television schedules, but six is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carried on a series of arches across a valley.

clue.text: Dressing viscountess, initially, in plumed headdress

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the first letter of viscountess
taken as written
an aigrette is a tuft of feathers worn on the head

explanation.surface: A noblewoman getting dressed, wearing a feathered headpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like putting on clothes but is a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette is a salad dressing of oil and vinegar.

clue.text: Boy on pitch wearing hat

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece being on another places it after that piece

blocks.note: pitch is a black tarry substance
a boy's name
someone in a coat is wearing it

explanation.surface: A lad out on a sports field has a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a playing field but is the black tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a waterproof sheet, a tarpaulin was a sailor's tarred hat, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Marvellous one, a character in Ugly Betty

blocks.note: fab is slang short for fabulous
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderful member of the cast of a television comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabia is a fashion-world figure in the American TV series Ugly Betty, played by Gina Gershon.

clue.text: Come close to rough

blocks.note: first meaning: the verb, to come near in value
second meaning: the adjective, not exact

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and adjective are spelt the same but said differently, stressing the last syllable for the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to nearly match; as an adjective it describes an estimate that is not precise.

clue.text: Write exam about county for Whitsuntide

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: to pen is to write
a test is an exam
Co is the abbreviation for county

explanation.surface: Set an exam paper on a county for the holiday period.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost is the Christian festival seven weeks after Easter, called Whitsun in Britain.

clue.text: Plotter studies airport surreptitiously

indicators.note: doing something surreptitiously means sneaking about, so these letters are covertly rearranged

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer secretly looks over an airport, perhaps planning a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is an old verb for studying closely, as in conning a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspirator is someone who joins in a secret scheme, so a plotter.

clue.text: Top university rented Juliet's house

blocks.note: a cap is a top or lid
U is the abbreviation for university
a let property is a rented one

explanation.surface: A first-rate college has leased the home where Juliet lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a family line, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet belongs to the Capulet family in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, house in the dynasty sense.

clue.text: All are drunk with auberge finally serving up traditional beer

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the last letter of auberge

explanation.surface: Everyone gets tipsy at a French inn that serves cask beer.
explanation.walkthrough: An auberge is a French inn. Real ale is the British term for cask-conditioned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is beer brewed and conditioned in the cask by traditional methods.

clue.text: Pester poor German

blocks.note: bad means poor in quality
Ger is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An instruction to nag an unfortunate man from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harass them with repeated demands.

clue.text: Level pegging on board in game

indicators.note: on board means inside a vessel, so one word sits within the abbreviation for a ship

blocks.note: level pegging means scores are even
SS, steamship, is the vessel one is on board

explanation.surface: Scores are tied on the board during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' signals the SS of a steamship, with the inner word placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a short form of rugby union played with seven players a side.

clue.text: Drink containing very soft fruit

indicators.note: containing means one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A beverage with some squishy fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very soft' seems to describe the fruit, but it is the musical marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Attendants argue dreadfully after note translated

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so these letters come out jumbled
translating changes words into a new form, so these letters take a new order
after tells us which piece is written second, following the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged first
the letters to be rearranged second

explanation.surface: Servants quarrel badly after a message has been rendered into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Trouble leading group

blocks.note: a team that is up is leading
a set is a group

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' looks like part of 'leading group', but it is a separate piece meaning ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to distress or bother them.

clue.text: Type of humour OK in G&S

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: the two letters of the abbreviation
to OK something is to allow it

explanation.surface: A kind of comedy that suits Gilbert and Sullivan operettas.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallows humour is grim joking about death or disaster, named after the hanging frame.

clue.text: Subjugate Eastern European in endless trap

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
a net is a trap
a Slav is a European from the east of the continent

explanation.surface: Forcing an Eastern European into bondage by catching them in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to subject them to servitude, so to subjugate them.

clue.text: Go round in foxtrot at 'Empress'

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Turning in a ballroom dance at a venue called the Empress.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about a centre, that is to spin or revolve.

clue.text: A capital city since about that time

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A city that has been the capital ever since a certain moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' belongs to the definition, though it looks like a letter for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece.
